 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The New York Yankees need help in the infield, and after Friday's non-tender deadline, some new faces could be hitting the open market.
 One name the Yankees should keep an eye on is St. Louis Cardinals infielder Nolan Gorman. Gorman can play second base and third base, but is blocked from regular playing time in the future in St. Louis. He is not exactly a star, but he's a player who would not hurt the Yankees to take a chance on.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Yankees have options at second base in Anthony Volpe and Luis García Jr. if Jazz Chisholm Jr. does sign elsewhere, as many expect him to. However, third base is a black hole for the Yankees, and they need to find a way to get rid of Ryan McMahon.
 Gorman can play third base, but he should not be expected to be the Yankees' final solution to the problem in the hot corner. However, he can be part of the solution.
 He's a decent defender who may just need a change of scenery to unlock some offense. He's a left-handed pull hitter who could take advantage of the short porch at Yankee Stadium. He pulls the ball in the air at one of the highest rates in the league.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In 2023, Gorman hit 27 home runs despite playing half of his games at Busch Stadium. He has a .645 OPS in three seasons since then and is expected to be non-tendered on Friday.
